channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Maine Collins-Jackson Debate Highlights Fight for Senate Control
item.description: The 73-year-old Republican incumbent faces one of her biggest tests yet in one of the most competitive races.
item.dc:creator: Steven T. Dennis

item.title: Top-Heavy Stock Rally Dares Bonds
item.description: Wall Street traders drove stocks to all-time highs on growing bets that Corporate America will be able to weather the threats from still-elevated energy costs and interest rates. Bloomberg Opinion's John Authers examines the market backdrop. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon talks AI, inflation, and government debt in conversation with Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie. Isabel Guzman, former SBA Administrator and Chair of the Global Risk Advisory Council, discusses their new Reputation Risk Index report. TIAA COO Sastry Durvasula joins to explain the firm's blueprint for implementing AI at scale. All on the latest episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says He’s Considering Gas Tax Suspension to Ease Costs
item.description: President Donald Trump said that he is weighing a potential suspension of the federal gas tax, as his administration looks for ways to ease high energy costs ahead of November’s midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Skylar Woodhouse and Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: Brazil Elections: Bolsonaro Secures Key Endorsement for Presidency
item.description: Brazil’s right-wing presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro secured the backing of veteran lawmaker Ronaldo Caiado on Tuesday as he moves to consolidate support from first-round rivals before a tight runoff.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho and Simone Iglesias

item.title: US Senate Map Moves in Democrats’ Favor as Kansas Rated ‘Tossup’
item.description: The Democratic Party’s path to controlling the US Senate continues to widen four weeks before Election Day, with once solidly conservative Kansas now considered a tossup race, the nonpartisan Cook Political Report said Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Steven T. Dennis

item.title: Election Administrators 'Confident' With Early Midterm Voting Underway, Says Morelle
item.description: New York Democrat Representative Joe Morelle said that despite scrutiny on election security, local and state election administrators are confident in election integrity with early voting already underway in some states. Morelle, who serves as the ranking member on the Committee on House Administration, said that lawmakers are willing to push back on any efforts taken by the DOJ to 'impair anyone's right to vote.' (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Four Weeks to Election Day
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the midterm elections. On today's show, Republican Congressman Brad Knott of North Carolina, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Democratic Congressman Joe Morelle of New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Cost of Heating, Housing at Center of Maine Senate Race
item.description: Brooke Sutherland, Bloomberg's Boston bureau chief, said that Maine residents are 'getting it at all ends' as they contend with 'acute' price increases for heating and housing ahead of the midterm elections. Sutherland expects cost of living to be a major topic at debates between Republican incumbent for Senate Susan Collins and her Democrat challenger Troy Jackson. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Lawmakers Urge Oz to Reconsider Remote Health Monitoring Rule
item.description: A bipartisan group of House lawmakers is urging the Trump administration to reconsider a rule that would ban third parties from remote health monitoring reimbursements under Medicare, arguing it would cripple health systems in rural communities.
item.dc:creator: Claire Bernard

item.title: GOP, Dems Pull Back Spending From North Carolina Senate Race
item.description: Republican Representative Brad Knott of North Carolina said Michael Whatley, the GOP nominee for Senate, is running against a "very tough" Democratic candidate but expects him to 'close the gap.' Knott, who serves on the House Homeland Security Committee, also discussed terror threats amid active conflicts in the MidEast and said that while there are 'absolutely terror cells in the United States,' the government is working to prevent them from operating in the US. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: GOP Shifts $5 Million to South Carolina Senate Race as Worries Mount
item.description: Republicans are bolstering US Senator Darline Graham’s campaign for a full term amid increasing concern that the race in South Carolina, traditionally a conservative stronghold, is tightening ahead of the Nov. 3 election.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason, Erik Wasson and Josh Wingrove

item.title: New Quebec Premier Seeks to Defy Polls and Separate Province From Canada
item.description: Quebec’s new leader, Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, says he won’t back down on his pledge to hold an independence referendum by 2030, despite polling that suggests most Quebecers aren’t on board.
item.dc:creator: Mathieu Dion

item.title: Quebec Separatists Win Power in New Challenge for Carney
item.description: The separatist Parti Québécois won Quebec’s election but fell short of a majority government, but they still represent a challenge for Prime Minister Mark Carney. Mathieu Dion explains what this means for Quebec's chances of secession and when Canada might be able to expect a vote for independence from its second largest province (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Iran Ramps Up Ship Attacks in Hormuz as Oil, Gas Flows Climb
item.description: Iran has increased the pace of attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz in recent days, just as oil shipments through the world’s most important energy chokepoint approach prewar levels.
item.dc:creator: Alex Longley, Ruth Liao and Grant Smith

item.title: How a Russian Boxer With Kremlin Ties Came to Bankroll Trump Jr.’s Wedding
item.description: Biker. Boxer. National Lottery czar. Business partner to Vladimir Putin’s chief bodyguard. And now: the man who helped pay for part of Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding celebration.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Drone Maker Anduril Pushes Into Subs With Maryland Factory
item.description: Anduril Industries, known for building drones and autonomous aircraft, is investing $3.7 billion to build a massive new shipbuilding facility in Maryland, a move that will enhance the US Navy’s nuclear-powered submarine production.
item.dc:creator: Jen Judson and Courtney McBride

item.title: Ireland Unveils €50,000 Tax Threshold for New Savings Scheme
item.description: Ireland’s new retail savings and investment accounts, aimed at encouraging more people to invest, will have a €50,000 ($56,318) tax-free threshold, Finance Minister Simon Harris announced in the budget Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Fletcher

item.title: Germany’s Ex-Intelligence Chief Arrested in Espionage Probe
item.description: Germany’s former foreign intelligence chief, August Hanning, was taken into custody as part of an investigation into treason and espionage allegations.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Donahue and Nick Heubeck

item.title: French School Protests Draw Over 250,000 as Violence Flares
item.description: Hundreds of French high schools were shut on Tuesday as teacher unions joined a student-led movement demanding more money for education that has spread across the country and sometimes turned violent.
item.dc:creator: Benoit Berthelot, William Horobin, Nayla Razzouk and Ania Nussbaum

item.title: Trump Says Terror Threats Forced B-1 Bombers Out of UK Base
item.description: President Donald Trump said fresh threats of terror attacks prompted the US to move its B-1 bombers from their base in the UK, contradicting his top diplomat who had earlier described the move as part of a regular rotation.
item.dc:creator: Courtney McBride and Ellen Milligan
